cards.text: Israel's dividing up the land of Canaan (Joshua 14:1), and now we get the allotment for the clans of the tribe of Judah. The south runs from the Salt Sea past Kadesh-barnea to the Brook of Egypt, the east is the Salt Sea, the north climbs right past the Jebusites at Jerusalem, and the west is the Great Sea. That border has more twists than the twist tie I shared a junk drawer with.

Then Joshua, Israel's leader, gives Caleb son of Jephunneh a portion among the sons of Judah: Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron. Caleb's the spy Moses once sent out, who asked for this hill country at eighty-five, still as strong for war as ever, even though the Anakim were there (Joshua 14:7-12).

cards.question: Joshua gives Caleb the city of Hebron. What is Joshua going by when he does it?
Hebron was once Kiriath-arba, and Arba was the forefather of Anak. Now Anak's descendants are there. What does Caleb do about them?

cards.text: From there Caleb marches against Debir, once known as Kiriath-sepher. Friend, after ONE big batch I need a nap, and this man just keeps going.

cards.question: Caleb says he will give his ___ in marriage to the man who strikes down Kiriath-sepher and captures it.

cards.text: And somebody steps up. Othniel, son of Caleb's brother Kenaz, captures the city.

cards.question: True or false: Once Othniel captures the city, Caleb backs out of his promise.
One day Caleb's daughter Acsah, now married to Othniel, urges Othniel to ask her father for a field. When she gets off her donkey, Caleb asks her something. What does he ask?

cards.text: "Give me a blessing," Acsah answers. Her father gave her land in the Negev, and now she asks for springs of water as well.

cards.question: True or false: Caleb gives his daughter Acsah both the upper and lower springs.

cards.text: Then comes the inheritance of the clans of Judah, city by city, each with its villages: the Negev down by Edom, the foothills, the hill country and the wilderness. Beersheba, Lachish, Hebron and En-gedi are all on the list, and so are Ekron, Ashdod and Gaza out by the Great Sea. Towns, villages, MORE towns. Judah's got more places than I've got chocolate chips, and friend, I've got a LOT of chocolate chips.
Back up north, Judah's border runs right past the Jebusites at Jerusalem. But the descendants of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites living there.

cards.question: The descendants of Judah can't drive the Jebusites out of Jerusalem. So how do things stand in Jerusalem when this was written?

answers.text: The Jebusites live among Judah's people
The city lies empty and in ruins
Judah's people have all moved away
